structured_output.summary: The draft covers all of B06: steering with the stick and d-pad mapped onto the existing steer range, both triggers, a dead-zone, and A to confirm on menus, with input merged into the same CarInput. Every criterion can be tested in Node through existing seams: createInput().read(), a mocked navigator.getGamepads, and the happy-dom game harness with requestAnimationFrame driven by hand. The overlap with #23 in src/game.ts is in different functions, so it is safe to build tonight. The only findings are minor notes for the builder.

findings.claim: The harness lint flags AC1 for naming navigator.getGamepads. That is the browser's public Gamepad API, not a repo internal, and tests have to mock it anyway. The criteria also use the combined input's read(), which is the exported createInput() seam that tests/input/keyboard.test.ts and touch.test.ts already pin. Neither name is a problem.
findings.suggestedFix: No change. Mock the pad through navigator.getGamepads with vi.stubGlobal, or define it on navigator, and read through createInput().read().

findings.claim: AC7 says 'the player's CarInput keeps steer 0', but CarInput isn't exposed by state(). During the countdown the car can't move, so that check would pass anyway.
findings.suggestedFix: Test AC7 in two ways. First, createInput().read() with only A held returns {steer:0, throttle:false, brake:false}. Second, in the game harness after GO, with A held and no other input, state().cars[0] matches a no-input race at the same tick, mode stays 'race' and paused stays false.

findings.claim: The backlog says 'A to confirm on menus', and the pause screen is a menu, but the draft leaves it out because the loop stops while paused. done_when only requires 'menus can be started with A', which RACE and NEXT RACE meet, so this is acceptable. Still, the owner may press A on the pause screen during the play-test and see nothing happen.
findings.suggestedFix: The builder must not quietly add pause support. Note the gap in the PR summary so the owner knows A doesn't resume yet. Pause support can be a follow-up item.

findings.claim: The menu A-poll has to run in frame() before the `mode !== 'race'` early return, because the loop keeps running on the menu but returns right away. Releases also have to be tracked across that path so the fresh-press rule in AC6 holds when the mode changes.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep one 'A was down last frame' flag that frame() updates on every call, whatever the mode. Fire only on a press edge, and only while an overlay is visible: the start screen, or the results screen once the player has finished.

findings.claim: #23 changes draw() and play() in src/game.ts. This draft touches frame() and the input wiring, which are different hunks.
findings.suggestedFix: Don't edit draw() or play(). Put the menu A-poll in frame() or a separate helper so either PR can rebase cleanly.

structured_output.overlapAssessment: #23 (countdown camera offset) changes src/game.ts only in draw(), where it adds a countdownClearance argument to scene.update, and in play(), where it changes a scene.update call. This draft adds gamepad polling inside createInput().read(), which is src/input, and a menu A-poll in frame() or a helper. That means different functions and different lines, and neither feature depends on the other's behaviour: gamepad input only changes the player's CarInput and menu activation, not the camera or the countdown. A textual conflict is unlikely, and if one happens it is a trivial rebase. Safe to build now.
